chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who vowed to walk to the House (Kaaba), and he passed by a crossing; he said, 'Let him stand at the crossing until he crosses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vowed to walk to the Kaaba but encounters a river?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *Yusr* (ease) in fulfilling vows, ruling that standing in the water at the crossing point suffices as 'walking' to the Kaaba, thereby avoiding unnecessary hardship (*Gharar*). This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on interpreting vows literally but reasonably, ensuring the vow's intent is met without imposing undue burden, a key concept in *Fiqh al-Nudhur*. The ruling underscores the balance between devotion and practicality, a theme frequently discussed by al-Tusi in his compilation of Imami legal traditions.
